interpretations: Group by `event.status`, average of the per-line difference (`amount` - `spent`), count of all joined budget lines with `spent` > 6.0
Group by `event.status`, average of `amount` minus average of `spent` (two separate averages), count of all joined budget lines with `spent` > 6.0
Group by `event.status`, average of the per-line difference (`amount` - `spent`), count only of lines where `amount` is non-null
Group by `event.status`, average of `budget.remaining` in place of `amount` - `spent`, count of all joined budget lines with `spent` > 6.0
Group by `event.status`, average of the per-line difference (`amount` - `spent`), count of distinct events with such budget lines
Group by `event.status`, average of the per-line difference (`amount` - `spent`), count of distinct `budget_id` values
Group by `budget.event_status` instead of `event.status`, average of (`amount` - `spent`), count of lines
Inner join between `budget` and `event`, with the `spent` > 6.0 filter applied before grouping (lines with no matching event dropped)
Inner join between `budget` and `event`, with the `spent` > 6.0 filter on the same lines as the count and the average
Result has one row per distinct `event.status` value, including a NULL status group if any matching events have a NULL status
Result has one row per distinct `event.status` value, excluding events with a NULL status
Average returned as NULL (blank) for a status where all `amount` values are NULL, with the count still including those lines
Average and count both restricted to lines where `amount` is non-null, so statuses with no such lines are omitted
SUM(`amount` - `spent`) divided by the count of all joined lines, so NULL `amount` lines count in the denominator
Group by `event.status`, average of `amount` (ignoring NULLs) minus average of `spent` computed only over lines where `amount` is non-null, count of all joined lines
queries:
SELECT e.status, AVG(b.amount - b.spent), COUNT(*)
FROM budget b
JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
WHERE b.spent > 6.0
GROUP BY e.status

SELECT e.status, AVG(b.amount) - AVG(b.spent), COUNT(CASE WHEN b.spent > 6.0 THEN 1 END)
FROM event e
JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
GROUP BY e.status
SELECT e.status, AVG(b.amount - b.spent) FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE b.amount IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.status

SELECT e.status, AVG(b.amount - b.spent), COUNT(*)
FROM event e
JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
WHERE b.spent > 6.0
GROUP BY e.status

SELECT e.status, AVG(b.amount - b.spent), COUNT(DISTINCT e.event_id)
FROM budget b
JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
GROUP BY e.status;

SELECT e.status, AVG(b.amount - b.spent), COUNT(DISTINCT b.budget_id)
FROM budget b
JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
GROUP BY e.status
